_about: How a phone's battery behaves, as data. The charge is reported three ways - MS.b(0x1000017) as a percent string, badger's device trait 17 as {status, level fraction, millivolts, plugged}, and app_log's power_percent - so all three have to come from one level, and that level has to move while a session runs. battery_section.py draws each install its starting level from this file and ChainReplay discharges it; neither holds numbers of its own.
_source: The recording's own three values disagree (94, 100 % on a charger, and 91: three moments of one launch), so none of them is 'the' battery and the recorded state is not reusable. The discharge and charge rates below are a phone's ordinary behaviour, stated as data rather than claimed as measurements of this model; the voltage curve is a lithium cell's resting voltage against charge, whose flat middle is why a phone sits near 3.8 V for most of a day.
_charging_share: the share of phones plugged in at any given moment
_level_when_charging: people plug in when it is getting low and unplug near full
_level_when_discharging: a triangular draw: a phone in someone's hand is more often part-way down than freshly full or nearly dead
_discharge_percent_per_hour: in use, with the screen on and the network busy
_standby_percent_per_hour: between launches, with the app closed
_redraw_after_hours: a longer gap than this and the phone has lived its own life since (charged, or not): a fresh level, rather than pretending to model the hours in between
_voltage_curve: [level as a fraction, millivolts] pairs, interpolated between, so any level gives a voltage that is not a round number
_charging_voltage_offset: a cell reads above its resting voltage while current is flowing into it
_voltage_jitter: the reading's own noise, either side, in millivolts
_cell_temperature: degrees Celsius. A cell sits a few degrees over the room while the screen is on, warmer again while it charges, and warms slowly over a session.
_status: android.os.BatteryManager's own constants: BATTERY_STATUS_CHARGING/_DISCHARGING and BATTERY_PLUGGED_AC
